title: The Reverse Sear Changed How I Cook Steak Forever
creator: Smoke & Salt with Joel
description:
Thick-cut ribeye, reverse seared: low oven, screaming hot cast iron, and a garlic butter baste. Recipe below.

Ingredients:
1 ribeye, 2 inches thick (about 600 g)
Kosher salt, black pepper
2 tbsp butter, 3 garlic cloves, thyme

Oven: 120 C / 250 F until 125 F internal, rest 10 minutes, sear 60-90 seconds per side.

The thermometer I use: https://meater.com/smokeandsalt (code SMOKE15)

sentences.t: This is a two-inch ribeye, and if you throw it straight into a hot pan, you're going to get a gray band all the way around and a raw middle.
So today we're doing a reverse sear, which basically means we cook it gently first and sear it last.
First thing, salt, and a lot of it.
I salted this last night and left it uncovered in the fridge, which dries out the surface so we get a better crust later.
If you didn't do that, even forty-five minutes ahead is fine, just don't salt it five minutes before, that's the worst of both worlds.
Cracked pepper, both sides, and onto a wire rack on a sheet pan.
The rack matters, because you want hot air all the way around the steak, not the bottom stewing in its own juice.
Oven's at two hundred and fifty Fahrenheit, that's about a hundred and twenty Celsius.
Now, the whole reverse sear lives or dies on temperature, so I'm putting the Meater probe in right now.
You want to push it in from the side, right into the thickest part, and past this little line on the probe.
Then in the app I'm picking ribeye, medium rare, and it sets a target of one twenty-five so I can pull it early and let carryover do the rest.
Into the oven, and now I don't have to open the door every ten minutes and let all the heat out.
Okay, it's been about thirty-five minutes, and you can see the app says we're at one eighteen, and it's estimating eight minutes left.
It also shows the ambient temperature in the oven, which is reading a bit low, so my oven runs cold, good to know.
And there's the alert, one twenty-five, so out it comes.
Now it rests for ten minutes, and while it does, I want to tell you about Meater, who are sponsoring this video.
It's a completely wireless probe, no cables trapped in the oven door, and the range is good enough that I can walk around the house.
It works for the oven, the grill, the smoker, even rotisserie.
If you want one, go to meater.com slash smokeandsalt and use code SMOKE15 for fifteen percent off.
I'll leave the link pinned in the comments too.
Okay, cast iron, and it needs to be smoking hot.
A little bit of high smoke point oil, I'm using beef tallow, but avocado oil works great too.
Steak goes in, and listen to that, that's what you want to hear.
Don't move it, just leave it for about a minute.
Flip, and look at that crust, edge to edge, that's because the surface was dry.
Now butter, garlic and thyme go in, and I'm tilting the pan and spooning that butter over the top, over and over.
This only takes thirty or forty seconds, we're not cooking it anymore, we're just flavoring the crust.
And I'll hold it on its side to render that fat cap, because nobody wants a chewy strip of fat.
Out of the pan, and because we already rested it before the sear, you can slice this pretty much straight away.
Against the grain, nice and thick.
And look at that, pink from edge to edge, basically no gray band at all.
That's the whole point of the reverse sear, the inside is perfectly even and the outside gets that crust.
A little flaky salt on top, and that's it.
Oh, that's so good.
Honestly, that's the best steak I've made in this kitchen.
If you try it, tag me, I want to see your crust.
Next week we're doing a whole smoked chicken, so make sure you're subscribed, and I'll see you then.
